reason: The text demonstrates the opposite: Israelites freely express their views throughout. Notable examples include: individual Israelites questioning the Gibeonites (וַיֹּאמֶר אִישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל), Joshua interrogating them directly, and most significantly, the entire congregation explicitly voicing complaints (וַיִּלֹּנוּ כָל־ הָעֵדָה עַל־ הַנְּשִׂיאִים) against the leaders' oath-keeping decision. The leaders then respond to defend their position. This passage exemplifies open dialogue and expressed disagreement with authority, not discouragement from speaking.
